page: Microsoft Azure B2als_v2 is a burstable virtual machine instance within the Basv2 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It features support for x86_64 instruction sets including AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, while omitting AVX-512 and AMX extensions. No integrated GPU hardware or local instance storage is bundled, requiring reliance on remote persistent storage volumes.

Benchmark metrics reflect strong single-core CPU throughput balanced against low aggregate execution and memory bandwidth capacity. In stress-ng evaluations, the single-core test reached 2700.69, ranking in the top quartile, whereas multi-core throughput registered identically at 2700.69, dropping into the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth metrics indicate constrained throughput, with 128.78 GB/sec for small cached reads, 35.05 GB/sec for large reads, and 24.18 GB/sec for uncached writes. Geekbench results show an average single-core score of 1479.0 and a multi-core score of 1807.0, with lower performance across Clang compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. Lightweight compression tasks achieved 25.94 GB/sec in gzip and 11.29 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3. Database and serving tests exhibited lower throughput, including 978.0 in PassMark database operations, 2.06 million Redis SET operations per second, and 2.58 GB/sec for static web serving.

The B2als_v2 provides an entry-level, budget-conscious profile by offering low memory allocation per vCPU and burstable compute capacity. Because compute allocation relies on a burstable credit architecture, sustained multi-core performance and continuous compute workloads will experience throttling once burst capacity is depleted. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage requires attached storage for operational file systems.

Given its single-threaded speed and burstable multi-core limits, Microsoft Azure B2als_v2 is suitable for low-intensity workloads with variable demand. Appropriate use cases include staging environments, light web servers, basic CI/CD test runners, small background worker services, and lightweight development tasks that do not require high memory density or sustained CPU execution.
description: The Microsoft Azure B2als_v2 is a burstable, entry-tier virtual machine belonging to the Basv2 family, driven by a 3.525 GHz AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Configured with 2 vCPUs sourced from a single physical core via multithreading and paired with 4.0 GB of system RAM, it maintains a lean 2.0 GB per core profile. The instance omits bundled local storage and GPU hardware, depending on attached network storage. Performance benchmarks demonstrate solid single-thread compute capabilities, achieving 2700.69 in stress-ng single-core tests, though overall multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth remain in the lower tiers due to core count constraints. Synthetic database and web serving tests reflect these limitations, with 2.58 GB/sec static web throughput and 2.06 million Redis operations per second. Offering a cost-conscious burstable compute profile, the B2als_v2 is tailored for lightweight workloads, staging environments, low-traffic web applications, and periodic task processing.
